research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official GOV.UK/Mining Remediation Authority, MHCLG Planning Data and British Geological Survey/UKRI verification; July 2026 currentness where available; mineral safeguarding/resource/permission separation, coalfield consultation and Coal Mining Risk Assessment triggers, mine-entry/workings uncertainty, permits/licences, subsidence claims, non-coal mining hazard, BritPits status, restoration/aftercare and NO_DATA provenance gates. Not parcel-level mineral, mining, ground-stability or development accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification plus repository duplicate searches

official_sources.name: GOV.UK minerals planning guidance
official_sources.fact: MHCLG minerals guidance separates mineral safeguarding, extraction permission, restoration, aftercare and review of old mineral permissions.
official_sources.gate: A Mineral Safeguarding Area or mineral resource is not a presumption that extraction will occur, and non-mineral development is not automatically refused.

official_sources.name: NPPF Chapter 17 sustainable use of minerals
official_sources.fact: NPPF requires safeguarding of mineral resources and infrastructure while expressly avoiding a presumption that safeguarded resources will be worked.
official_sources.gate: Safeguarding policy is a planning input, not a parcel-level extraction right or automatic development prohibition.

official_sources.name: Planning practice guidance land stability
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance identifies subsidence, ground heave, mining records and qualified stability assessment as relevant to development.
official_sources.gate: Potential instability is not proof of actual parcel failure; planning, building regulations, mining liability and engineering evidence remain distinct.

official_sources.name: Natural England mineral-site agricultural reclamation advice
official_sources.fact: Natural England guidance requires restoration planning, soil-resource evidence and typically a five-year agricultural aftercare programme where appropriate.
official_sources.gate: A restoration strategy is not evidence that restoration is complete or that the site is immediately developable for a new afteruse.

official_sources.name: Mining Remediation Authority planning advice service
official_sources.fact: Updated 25 June 2026, the service supports proposals in Development High Risk Areas on the coalfield.
official_sources.gate: Using or obtaining planning advice is not a planning permission, Coal Mining Risk Assessment approval or guarantee of safe and stable development.

official_sources.name: MRA detailed Development High Risk Area planning advice
official_sources.fact: MRA states its advice is limited to coal-mining legacy features and cannot prejudge or guarantee the local planning authority decision.
official_sources.gate: Professional advice must not be converted into an approval, planning decision or permanent risk clearance.

official_sources.name: Coal Mining Risk Assessments guidance
official_sources.fact: Most development in a Development High Risk Area requires a Coal Mining Risk Assessment with appropriate evidence.
official_sources.gate: High-risk-area membership is a trigger for assessment, not proof that a specific parcel is unstable or undevelopable.

official_sources.name: Access coal mining information and data
official_sources.fact: Published 16 July 2026, MRA guidance lists free and paid access routes to coal records, abandonment plans, licences, deeds and detailed searches.
official_sources.gate: Archive availability or a broad-area record is not parcel-specific current ground-condition evidence without exact search and plan matching.

official_sources.name: Coal mining information and data collection
official_sources.fact: MRA publishes free, licensed and historical coal-mining information routes, including map viewing and historical records.
official_sources.gate: A collection index is provenance evidence, not a complete parcel-level mining search.

official_sources.name: Coal mining data: mine entries
official_sources.fact: MRA documents the national mine-entry dataset showing known entrances into mine workings.
official_sources.gate: A mapped mine entry is not an exact surveyed shaft condition, ownership right, remediation status or development exclusion without current site evidence.

official_sources.name: Coal mining records data deeds and documents
official_sources.fact: MRA holds extensive historical coal-mining data, plans and property documents and provides routes for access.
official_sources.gate: Historic records can be incomplete or time-specific and must not be treated as a current engineering conclusion.

official_sources.name: Coal mining data: licence areas
official_sources.fact: MRA's licence-area dataset identifies areas associated with licences for working coal.
official_sources.gate: Licence-area geometry is not proof of extraction, current operations, planning permission or parcel instability.

official_sources.name: Apply to license coal mining data
official_sources.fact: MRA explains licensable coal datasets and confirms Mining Remediation Authority is the trading name while Coal Authority remains the legal name.
official_sources.gate: Availability under licence is not evidence that a parcel has been checked or affected.

official_sources.name: Coal mining data: shallow coal workings
official_sources.fact: MRA identifies known underground coal workings at depths of 30 metres or less.
official_sources.gate: Shallow-working presence is a hazard input, not proof of current subsidence or a development refusal.

official_sources.name: Coal mining data: coal outcrops
official_sources.fact: MRA identifies locations where workable coal seams are at or close to the surface.
official_sources.gate: Coal outcrop geometry does not prove extraction, ownership, planning status or current instability.

official_sources.name: Coal mining data: coalfield consultation area
official_sources.fact: The dataset shows the known extent of coal-mining activity used to identify possible ground instability and mining hazards.
official_sources.gate: Consultation-area coverage is a screening/consultation trigger, not a parcel-level hazard finding.

official_sources.name: Free of charge coal mining information
official_sources.fact: MRA provides selected coal-mining information through a free map viewer and web mapping services.
official_sources.gate: Free map-viewer layers are screening information and do not replace a formal mining report or site investigation where required.

official_sources.name: Mining Remediation Authority metadata collection
official_sources.fact: MRA publishes technical metadata for multiple national coal-mining datasets.
official_sources.gate: Metadata describes dataset purpose and limitations; it is not itself parcel evidence.

official_sources.name: Coal mining data: fissures and breaklines
official_sources.fact: MRA documents geological disturbances that may have been affected by coal mining.
official_sources.gate: A recorded fissure or breakline does not establish current movement, exact causation or structural impact at a parcel.

official_sources.name: Get a permit to deal with coal or coal mines
official_sources.fact: Updated 1 April 2026, MRA requires permits for specified works affecting coal, mine workings or mine entries.
official_sources.gate: A permit application, need for a permit, or engineering appraisal is not a granted permit or planning permission.

official_sources.name: Coal mining permits and licences
official_sources.fact: MRA distinguishes permits to disturb coal or mines from licences/consents for coal mining and related activities.
official_sources.gate: Permit, licence, planning permission and land rights are separate regimes and must not be collapsed into one approval.

official_sources.name: Check if property is affected by coal mining
official_sources.fact: GOV.UK provides a route to check coal-mining effects and order property-specific reports.
official_sources.gate: A free area check or map result is not equivalent to the full paid report or a geotechnical investigation.

official_sources.name: Claim for subsidence damage caused by coal mining
official_sources.fact: GOV.UK describes the process for coal-mining subsidence damage claims and engineering inspection.
official_sources.gate: A claim, reported cracking or an inspection request is not proof that coal mining caused the damage or that a claim will be accepted.

official_sources.name: Mining Remediation Authority about us
official_sources.fact: MRA manages legacy coal-mining effects, subsidence claims, mine-water pollution and coal licensing responsibilities.
official_sources.gate: Organisational responsibility does not prove a specific parcel is affected by a managed hazard or liability.

official_sources.name: Mining Remediation Authority framework document
official_sources.fact: The framework states the Coal Authority operates as Mining Remediation Authority and sets out statutory mining-remediation duties.
official_sources.gate: Statutory responsibility is not parcel-specific hazard, title or consent evidence.

official_sources.name: MRA permit process guidance notes
official_sources.fact: MRA permit guidance explains permit terms, engineering evidence and indemnity arrangements for works affecting coal interests.
official_sources.gate: Permit terms or indemnity requirements are not evidence that works have been approved or completed.

official_sources.name: MRA Technical Guidance Note TGN01/2019
official_sources.fact: TGN01 records lessons from a major subsidence event and is relevant to planners, surveyors, developers and geotechnical specialists.
official_sources.gate: A case-study mechanism must not be assumed to occur at another parcel without site-specific evidence.

official_sources.name: Coal mining licence applications supporting documents
official_sources.fact: MRA publishes supporting guidance for coal-mining licence applications including subsidence-security information.
official_sources.gate: Application documents are not a granted licence, planning permission or evidence that operations have commenced.

official_sources.name: Available coal mining data sets
official_sources.fact: Updated 1 April 2026, the catalogue lists mine entries, mine gas, probable workings, shallow workings, site investigations, underground workings and other datasets.
official_sources.gate: Dataset availability or a dataset name does not establish a positive record at a target site.

official_sources.name: Surface Coal Resource Metadata
official_sources.fact: Surface coal resource areas indicate resources potentially capable of surface extraction and support mineral safeguarding.
official_sources.gate: Resource geometry is not planning permission, economic viability or proof that extraction will occur.

official_sources.name: Coal mining data: surface resource areas
official_sources.fact: The dataset describes coal resources potentially capable of extraction by surface mining methods.
official_sources.gate: Resource-area coverage must not be promoted to current operation, ownership or consent status.

official_sources.name: Surface Coal Mining Metadata
official_sources.fact: Surface-mining areas denote past or current surface excavations but the metadata warns the polygons do not necessarily reflect exact excavation extent.
official_sources.gate: Historic/snapshot polygons are not exact current excavation boundaries or residual-risk measurements.

official_sources.name: Coal mining data: surface coal mining
official_sources.fact: The dataset covers areas of coal extracted by surface excavations in the past or currently being excavated.
official_sources.gate: A dataset hit does not by itself identify current operator, restoration completion, permission status or exact parcel extent.

official_sources.name: Abandoned Mines Catalogue Metadata
official_sources.fact: The catalogue indexes the spatial coverage of deposited abandoned mine plans for surface and deep workings.
official_sources.gate: Catalogue coverage identifies relevant plans; it is not a surveyed parcel boundary or proof that all historic workings are recorded.

official_sources.name: Probable coal mine workings user guide
official_sources.fact: Probable workings represent estimated extents where mining is likely although no recorded plan exists.
official_sources.gate: Probable workings must remain probabilistic and must not be converted into exact mined geometry.

official_sources.name: Prices of licensable coal mining data
official_sources.fact: Updated 2026 pricing lists the licensable coal datasets and distinguishes available data products.
official_sources.gate: Pricing/catalogue information is not parcel evidence and no paid dataset was required for this research wave.

official_sources.name: Coal Authority data and information plan 2024 to 2027
official_sources.fact: The plan describes ongoing digitisation and publication of historic mining information including abandoned-mine plans.
official_sources.gate: Future digitisation commitments do not imply present completeness of online records.

official_sources.name: Coal outcrops user guide
official_sources.fact: The user guide explains coal-outcrop definitions and transfer of information from historical source plans into the national database.
official_sources.gate: Plan-derived positional information must retain source accuracy limits and cannot be treated as survey-grade parcel geometry.

official_sources.name: Fissures and breaklines user guide
official_sources.fact: The user guide defines fissures and breaklines and documents their derivation from historical mining and mapping records.
official_sources.gate: Recorded disturbance does not establish live movement or exact building-level impact.

official_sources.name: Monitoring Points Metadata
official_sources.fact: Monitoring-point metadata records measurements such as water level, mine gas, flow, chemistry and pumping data at managed points.
official_sources.gate: A monitoring point or mine-water dataset is not a parcel-wide groundwater or gas condition measurement.

official_sources.name: BGS mineral resources dataset
official_sources.fact: BGS mineral resources data maps the geological distribution of onshore mineral resources at 1:50,000 scale.
official_sources.gate: Geological resource mapping is not a mineral safeguarding area, planning permission or proof of viable extraction.

official_sources.name: BGS onshore mineral resource maps
official_sources.fact: BGS county mineral-resource maps combine resource, extraction, permission and selected designation information for planning support.
official_sources.gate: Many maps are historic planning baselines and must not be treated as current local-plan policy or current permission status.

official_sources.name: BGS MineralsUK planning portal
official_sources.fact: MineralsUK links planning, construction minerals, industrial minerals, policy, factsheets and resource maps.
official_sources.gate: A planning-information portal is not an authoritative parcel decision or local mineral-plan policy map.

official_sources.name: BGS mineral safeguarding good practice advice
official_sources.fact: BGS good-practice advice explains how Mineral Safeguarding Areas can be defined and national safeguarding policy implemented.
official_sources.gate: Good-practice methodology is not the adopted MSA boundary for an individual mineral planning authority.

official_sources.name: BGS mineral planning factsheets
official_sources.fact: BGS factsheets provide commodity-level information on supply, resources, reserves and planning issues, with some factsheets updated in 2025.
official_sources.gate: National commodity evidence is not site-specific resource quality, reserve, permission or viability.

official_sources.name: BGS industrial minerals planning
official_sources.fact: BGS describes industrial-mineral planning and supporting resource/permission mapping.
official_sources.gate: Industrial-mineral importance does not imply a parcel contains a viable deposit or should be worked.

official_sources.name: BGS construction minerals planning
official_sources.fact: BGS describes construction minerals and the managed aggregates supply evidence base.
official_sources.gate: Regional/national aggregates supply need is not parcel-specific planning permission or extraction feasibility.

official_sources.name: BGS minerals legislation and policy
official_sources.fact: BGS explains that mineral extraction generally needs planning permission and that safeguarding and restoration are distinct planning concepts.
official_sources.gate: BGS policy summary does not replace operative legislation, adopted local plans or site-specific permissions.

official_sources.name: BGS mining hazard not including coal coverage
official_sources.fact: BGS 1:50,000 mining-hazard data indicates potential hazard from recorded non-coal underground workings.
official_sources.gate: Hazard coverage is not an assessment of actual instability at a parcel and excludes coal-mining evidence.

official_sources.name: BGS BritPits dataset
official_sources.fact: BritPits records active, inactive, dormant and ceased mines, quarries and other mineral operations with point/location attributes.
official_sources.gate: A BritPits point or operational-status field is not an exact planning-permission boundary, mineral safeguarding boundary or parcel hazard zone.

official_sources.name: Planning Data mineral safeguarding area dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data currently reports 0 mineral-safeguarding-area records, 0 providers and no collection attempt.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform records are a data-availability state, not proof that a parcel lies outside every adopted Mineral Safeguarding Area.
